benchmark_context.provenance: Supplied audited measurements, not rerun here
benchmark_context.interpretation: Allocation is faster than GNU in the supplied cross-runtime row, yet regresses against OLD at the matched smaller count. Do not extrapolate either row to all sizes or diagnose the regression from timings alone.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: SBCL allocates key/value pairs separately from bucket indexes and next links; hash storage is conditional on custom or structural tests. Default empty tables defer storage.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen prelude 4283-4320 already has pairs/hash/next/index vectors, no per-entry cons. Native helper 19770-19804 already extracts backing bases once.
claims.proposal: INFERENCE/PROPOSED: represent indexed loads, packed integer arrays, owner identity and shape proofs in general memory IR so ordinary Lisp hash code receives the same optimizations. Do not add another native gethash arm.
claims.invariants: Existing table/image layout remains versioned; nil key differs from vacancy; all values remain traced.
claims.acceptance: Verify identical semantics across ordinary compiled Lisp and reference paths, including empty tables, nil keys/values, old images and direct/legacy representation.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: general SBCL hash tables use bucket heads and next-vector chains; bucket selection masks a hash against power-of-two bucket count. This is not evidence for a Swiss-table/open-addressed layout.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen build 19689-19692 uses multiplicative reduction; 19770-19804 follows next links. Existing code already avoids hash/next base extraction until first key mismatch.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: teach general compiler unsigned multiply/truncate, mask, induction and address calculation before considering a layout change. Alternative open addressing requires separate deletion/weakness proof and migration cost.
claims.invariants: Hash reduction must match unsigned width and reference equality; collision chains cannot silently terminate early.
claims.acceptance: Adversarial collisions, misses, negative and large hash returns, and deletion/reinsertion; collect chain lengths and bytes per entry.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: SBCL chooses getter/setter/remover families by eq/eql/equal/equalp/custom state and synchronization. ht-hash-setup invokes custom hash functions dynamically.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen build nl_ht_test_mode near 19383 caches test mode in metadata; custom functions remain in descriptor; prelude 4400-4430 snapshots test/hash closures and guards mutations.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: guarded type/shape specialization and devirtualization in universal compiler IR, with a semantic fallback for dynamic calls. Do not import SBCL safety-0 assumptions into Emacs Lisp.
claims.invariants: Preserve wrong-type signals, dynamic call/redefinition policy, custom hash/equality callbacks, recursive reads and mutation rejection with unwind restoration.
claims.acceptance: Callback signals and GC, recursive lookup, callback mutation attempts, changed symbol functions, mixed fixnum/float/symbol keys.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: define-gethash/flat linearly scans pairs with specialized eq/eql comparisons; grow-hash-table keeps a small-table flat regime before chains.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen prelude always constructs its documented backing-vector schema; small-table distribution in measured workload is UNKNOWN.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED alternative: compact small-table representation, only if census shows enough small tables. Prefer first compiling ordinary bounded loops efficiently; representation polymorphism adds guard and migration cost.
claims.invariants: Threshold transition preserves key identity, weakness, counts and custom callbacks; no benchmark-specific threshold.
claims.acceptance: Size sweep around every transition, creation/empty-table memory and total runtime, mixed read/write workloads.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: grow-hash-table allocates new storage, may reuse the index vector when hashes remain valid, and separates pair capacity from bucket sizing.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen prelude nelisp--hash-resize 4295-4320 copies pairs and metadata then reconstructs chains; existing growth policy is not absent.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: general bulk-copy IR with overlap/GC ownership contracts and explicit publication of replacement storage; consider independent capacities only with measured memory benefit.
claims.invariants: No stale interior pointers across allocating resize; failure before publication leaves a usable old table; callback-visible semantics preserved.
claims.acceptance: Resize with collisions, forced allocation failure/GC where supported, image reload, count and all entries checked.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: define-remhash unlinks chain head or predecessor and calls clear-slot; GC/movement status is checked if a miss may be stale.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen prelude nelisp--hash-custom-rem 4474-4489 already clears key/value/hash and returns slot to freelist.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: retain Lisp deletion algorithm; compiler combines checked vector operations under a valid table proof rather than a new native deletion implementation.
claims.invariants: Delete removes GC reachability and retains chain/free-list integrity; do not add tombstones to chaining design.
claims.acceptance: Head/middle/tail deletion, absent removal, churn, weak-key retention and count/free-slot integrity.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: collector scans hash pairs and sets the rehash bit when an address-sensitive key moves; Lisp rehash can recompute address hashes while retaining stable stored hashes.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen build nl_ht_identity_key_hash 19629-19633 uses bf_identity_hash; nl_ht_identity_sync before 19770 checks arena epoch/meta identity and can reindex. Do not call current identity hashing movement-oblivious.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: make identity-hash stability and relocation epochs explicit object-representation/GC ABI contracts. Alternatives: stable per-object identity or relocation-triggered rehash; former adds storage, latter adds repair latency.
claims.invariants: Equal identity before/after move; no stale raw address or duplicate key after compaction, image relocation or callback GC.
claims.acceptance: Force relocation between insert/lookup/delete, verify all entries and identity hashes under legacy and direct representations.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: SBCL defines four weakness implications and weak operations pin keys, transfer culled cells, find entries and use recursive locking when synchronized.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen hash metadata stores weakness at prelude 4287; complete native weak fixed-point collector analysis is UNKNOWN in this bounded read.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: compiler treats weak storage accesses as GC-sensitive operations; use NeLisp/Emacs weakness semantics, not CL labels as a replacement specification.
claims.invariants: Preserve ephemeron/fixed-point behavior, cycles and callback liveness; ordinary vector tracing cannot substitute for weak tracing.
claims.acceptance: GNU parity for every supported weakness mode, cycles and chains of dependent weak entries; negative controls that retain or drop an entry incorrectly.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: emit-allocation reads per-thread cons/mixed TLAB free/end slots, checks prospective end, updates free pointer and tags result; overflow calls an allocator trampoline and large objects bypass the per-thread region.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen build nl_chunk_try_alloc 6205-6224 already performs CAS bump reservation; nl_cons_alloc 4080-4100 already uses typed-block free/next cell paths, falling back during parallel allocation. src/nelisp-allocator.el nursery is not evidence of the measured executable's chosen allocator.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: general allocate-object IR lowered to current typed region fast path; optional per-thread regions only after measuring shared CAS/refill costs. No claim that NeLisp lacks bump allocation.
claims.invariants: Nonoverlapping aligned ranges, overflow before publication, GC accounting and parallel fallback; unused TLAB tails must remain walkable and roots published at safepoints.
claims.acceptance: Single/multi-thread allocation, exhaustion/refill, small/large objects, forced collection; count bytes, CAS retries, refills, unused tails and peak RSS.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: lisp_alloc checks alignment, handles TLAB capacity and slow-path statistics, and accounts large allocations toward GC triggers.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen nl_alloc_bytes_uncheck 6228-6263 charges GC debt, tries free lists, zeroes reused memory, then CAS-bumps or adds chunk. Checked wrapper nl_alloc_bytes begins 1282.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: describe allocates/may-GC/may-signal and size/alignment on memory IR; retain one explicit slow boundary for replenishment, checking and GC debt, rather than hide it behind an allegedly pure primitive.
claims.invariants: Accounting includes reuse, failure and typed fast paths; checked allocator behavior remains selectable; compiler cannot hoist across possible GC/signals without proof.
claims.acceptance: Exact accounting and live-data survival on each slow exit, failed refill and checked mode; negative control skips debt charging.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: emit-alloc-other computes object header from word count/widetag, allocates padded bytes and stores header while allocating; lowtag is combined with allocation result.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen arena-source header access 5672-5676 masks block total/marks; typed cons builder 4064-4100 uses side marks. Current layout is mixed, not uniformly headered.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: define object family, traced slots, size, tag, initialization and publication in universal allocation IR; maintain descriptor/version compatibility for typed and legacy objects.
claims.invariants: Collector sees only valid initialized shapes; tag does not replace owner root; image/reload and conservative pointer recognition agree.
claims.acceptance: Heap walk after each allocation family, image dump/load, header corruption negative controls and direct/legacy parity.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: SBCL comments explicitly say all pages except CONS are prezeroed in this gencgc path; initialization safety is tied to pseudo-atomic allocation. This is not universal permission to omit initialization.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen nl_alloc_zero_fill 6158-6169 writes reused blocks; nl_alloc_bytes_uncheck invokes it on reuse. Typed-block initialization has different rules.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: definite-initialization and no-publication regions may eliminate only proven redundant stores. Alternative page prezeroing moves cost to refill; compare total work and dirty pages.
claims.invariants: Every traced slot valid before collection/publication; Lisp-visible default elements correct; stale payload cannot retain objects or expose old bytes.
claims.acceptance: Reuse poisoned blocks, collect at supported boundaries, verify default vectors/conses and peak retained bytes; include zero-fill byte counters.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: scavenge_root_gens uses page write-protection/cleanliness to avoid rescanning older pages with no old-to-young pointers. This depends on the collector's page protocol.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen typed GC builder 4500 onward has per-block mark bits; bounded analysis does not establish equivalent generational remembered-set behavior. Existing allocator module's nursery comments do not establish live runtime generation semantics.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: retain abstract traced-store/barrier effect in memory IR now; introduce generational collection as a separate project with remembered sets, safepoints and roots, not as an allocator micro-optimization.
claims.invariants: Every old-to-young store, including raw/vector/closure/global writes, participates; weak edges use their own protocol; no allocation benchmark alone validates GC.
claims.acceptance: Promote parent, store young child through every store family, drop other roots and minor collect; omission-of-barrier negative control must fail.

claims.fact: OBSERVED: emit-allocation is documented for use inside pseudo-atomic allocation and emit-alloc-other performs header initialization through allocating. Weak hash paths explicitly pin keys.
claims.nelisp_anchor/currentlimits: Frozen hash finder 19770-19804 caches raw interior bases and calls comparators. Complete transitive may-GC behavior of these DSL calls is UNKNOWN here; no assertion of an actual dangling-pointer bug.
claims.proposal: PROPOSED: general compiler owner/interior-pointer relation and explicit may-GC safepoints; either prohibit collection within a proven raw-address scope or root owners and recompute addresses after safepoints.
claims.invariants: Signals/unwind and callbacks invalidate assumptions as specified; no raw interior pointer survives relocation without owner/recomputation; use NeLisp ABI, not SBCL pseudo-atomic machine protocol verbatim.
claims.acceptance: Force GC inside equality/hash callbacks and allocation slow paths, move owners, verify lookup; intentionally missing-root negative control must fail.

phased_gates: P0: preserve supplied source/binary/driver hashes and qualify benchmark provenance separately; profile ordinary workloads and census table sizes/allocation families before choosing layout or TLAB changes.

P1: add general memory/allocation IR with explicit type/shape guards, traced stores, owner lifetimes, may-GC/may-signal effects and initialization/publication; reference-path semantic parity and broken-input controls first.

P2: compile Lisp hash/allocator-facing loops through that IR; verify no added speed-only native primitives; exercise custom callbacks, mutation, weakness, images, checked allocator, direct and legacy shapes.
P3: only then evaluate optional packed hash indexes, small-table layout, TLABs or page prezeroing independently; moving/generational collection remains a separate acceptance boundary.

P4 end-to-end: same N, same inputs/results and driver across GNU bytecode/OLD/NEW, fixed CPU/warmups and alternating fresh processes, per-N samples, binary/source hashes; report elapsed distribution, total allocated bytes/objects, live bytes after GC, collection count/time, RSS, refill/CAS/zero-fill metrics. Include actual package/workload behavior and all semantic gates; no speed target is promised.
